programme: Mestrado em Produção e Tecnologias do Som (Master in Sound Production and Technologies)
stillExists: YES — listed with live 2026/27 application phases on the university's own programme page.
awards: Real second-cycle master's. 'Mestrado' in Produção e Tecnologias do Som, 4 semestres / 120 ECTS, regime presencial (Lisbon).
acceptsQuote: Conditions of access list 'titulares de grau de licenciado ou equivalente legal' and holders of foreign first-cycle degrees aligned with Bologna; a further route admits those whose 'currículo escolar, científico ou profissional' is recognised as adequate. The page names graduates 'nas áreas da musicologia e tecnologias do som, realização e produção audiovisual e artes digitais' as the target audience, but does not make a music degree a condition.
liveAudition: NO — no audition and no performance test. Selection is documentary: 25% weight on the prior qualification, 75% on interview plus portfolio assessment (100% interview for candidates without a degree). This is a portfolio review + interview, not an audition.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — the public programme page states a portfolio is assessed (75% of the score together with the interview) but publishes no specification of number of works, duration or file format. Tried the programme page and its candidatura sub-pages; the /propinas sub-page returns HTTP 404. He would have to email the coordinator for the spec.
tunisianCost: Private university, single rate — no separate non-EU tariff is published. Published charges: candidatura (application) EUR 460, or EUR 180 reduced; inscrição/matrícula EUR 350; propina EUR 12.68 per ECTS; seguro escolar EUR 50. At 12.68 EUR/ECTS x 120 ECTS the degree's tuition component is about EUR 1,522 in total, i.e. roughly EUR 760/yr — but the page also expresses this as approx. EUR 380.40 per 30 ECTS, and Lusófona normally bills in monthly instalments, so the annual figure needs written confirmation.
funding: UNVERIFIED at programme level. No scholarship for non-EU master's applicants is advertised on this page. Portugal has no general non-EU master's scholarship he would automatically win. Treat as self-funded.
deadline: 2026/27 cycle (PRIOR CYCLE pattern for him): 18 July – 1 September 2026. Expect an equivalent July–September window in 2027; nothing for 2027/28 is published yet.
language: Portuguese. No English track is offered. He has no Portuguese.
verdictWhy: The gate is genuinely soft — no audition, an open degree rule, and cheap by European standards — but the whole degree is taught in Portuguese, a language he does not have and would need to reach academic level in within twelve months. There is no funding attached and the application fee alone is EUR 460 (EUR 180 reduced), which is real money for a programme he could not follow. Revisit only if he commits to a year of Portuguese first.
correction: Input listed the cost band as 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr'. That is plausible for the tuition line (EUR 12.68/ECTS) but the input omits the EUR 460 application fee and the EUR 350 enrolment fee, which together exceed a year of tuition. Input also listed the gate as 'Portfolio + exam/interview'; there is no exam — it is portfolio + interview only.

institution: Universitatea Națională de Artă Teatrală și Cinematografică „I.L. Caragiale“ București (UNATC), Facultatea de…
programme: Arta sunetului de film (The Art of Film Sound), studii universitare de masterat
stillExists: YES — 'Arta sunetului de film' is running with a published 2026/2027 admission calendar and is listed in the UNATC Senate fee schedule for 2026-2027.
awards: Real second-cycle master's (studii universitare de masterat), 2 years, 120 ECTS, awarded by a state arts university.
acceptsQuote: 'Candidaţii trebuie să fi absolvit o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite' — any 180- or 240-credit bachelor. No music or film field is named as a condition.
liveAudition: NO live performance audition. Two graded components (each 1–10, pass mark 6.00), single stage: Proba 1 written — 'Probă de cultură cinematografică pe baza bibliografiei de concurs și testarea cunoștințelor tehnice în domeniul designului de sunet'; Proba 2 oral — 'Colocviu pe baza unei lucrări din portofoliu, la alegerea candidatului. Candidatul se va prezenta la această probă și cu proiectul DAW'. So: a written film-culture/technical exam plus a portfolio defence. Both are sat in person in Bucharest ('Susținerea probelor de concurs va avea loc „față în față” (fizic)' is the UNMB wording; UNATC likewise schedules on-site exam dates).
portfolioSpec: 'un portofoliu ce va conține lucrări artistice cu design sonor realizat de către candidat (portofoliul poate include copii digitale după filme sau alte proiecte relevante din domeniul designului sonor pentru film și media)'. No number of works, no duration and no file format is prescribed. Decisive extra: for Proba 2 he must bring the editable DAW session ('proiectul DAW') of the one work he defends — not just a bounced file. Build brief: several finished pieces of sound design to picture, with at least one whose full session he can open and explain.
tunisianCost: Tuition 13.750 lei/an for 'Arta sunetului de film' (Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290, Anexa 1, II.2 MASTER – FACULTATEA DE FILM), about EUR 2,750/yr. Admission registration fee 400 lei ('Taxă de înscriere la concursul de admitere la studii universitare de master pentru toate programele de studii din cadrul celor două facultăți — 400 lei'). The Senate document contains NO separate euro tariff for non-EU citizens; whether OG 22/2009's currency minimum for non-EU own-account students is applied on top is UNVERIFIED — the UNATC foreign-citizens page publishes no euro figure either. He must ask the Serviciul Relații Internaționale in writing. Note 3 budget (free) places exist but budget places are contested by Romanian and EU candidates on the same exam.
funding: Two separate, earlier applications, neither automatic on admission: (1) Romanian MFA scholarship via scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro — but at master's level it funds studies in Romanian, and requires a Letter of Acceptance first; window approx. 16 Feb – 31 Mar (PRIOR CYCLE 2026). (2) ARICE call, 40 places, approx. 11 May – 12 June (PRIOR CYCLE 2026), priority fields. Neither is granted by UNATC itself and both close months before the September exam, so he would have to run the scholarship application and the admission in parallel a year ahead.
language: Romanian. The programme is not in the English-taught list — UNATC's English master's programmes are Design for New Media, Visual effects, Audiovisual Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts and Art of Game design (all marked '(lb.engleză)' in the fee annex); 'Arta sunetului de film' is not among them. Non-EU applicants must either complete the Romanian preparatory year or present a certificate 'de nivel minim B1 ... eliberate de instituţiile de învăţământ superior acreditate din România ... de lectoratele de limbă ... sau de Institutul Cultural Român'. The written exam is on a Romanian film-culture bibliography.
deadline: 2026/2027 (PRIOR CYCLE, use as the pattern): enrolment 4 August – 9 September 2026; document verification 10–11 September; exams 15–20 September 2026. A separate non-EU date exists for the English-taught master's ('Data examenului de admitere pentru candidații non-UE, la programele de master în limba engleză, este 01 septembrie') — which does not cover this Romanian-taught programme.
verdictWhy: This is the best-shaped gate on the whole list for him — no audition, any 180/240-credit bachelor accepted, a portfolio of his own sound work plus a DAW session, and tuition of only about EUR 2,750/yr. The blocker is Romanian: the programme is taught in Romanian, the written exam is on a Romanian bibliography, and as a Tunisian he must produce a B1 Romanian certificate from a recognised issuer or do a preparatory year. Resolve the Romanian-language route (ICR certificate or preparatory year, which pushes entry to 2028) before spending anything else on it.
correction: Input said cost 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr'. Wrong — the Senate schedule sets 'Arta sunetului de film' at 13.750 lei/yr, about EUR 2,750/yr, plus a 400-lei registration fee. Input also said gate 'Portfolio only'. Wrong — there is a compulsory written exam (Proba 1) on a Romanian film-culture bibliography and technical sound-design knowledge, sat in person, in addition to the portfolio colloquium.

institution: Ankara Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Üniversitesi (Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, MGÜ)
programme: Müzik Teknolojileri Tezli Yüksek Lisans Programı (Music Technologies, thesis master) — Müzik Teknolojileri Ana Bilim Da…
stillExists: YES — the Müzik Teknolojileri Tezli Yüksek Lisans programme is running; MGÜ published a 2026-2027 güz yarıyılı graduate intake announcement with applications 10–24 August 2026.
awards: Real second-cycle degree: 'Tezli Yüksek Lisans' (thesis master) in Müzik Teknolojileri, under the Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü, Müzik Teknolojileri Ana Bilim Dalı.
acceptsQuote: Sınav Kılavuzu, section 3 Başvuru Şartları, column 'Programa Kabul edilen Mezunlar': 'Herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak' — graduating from ANY undergraduate programme. No ALES required ('ALES Puanı Şartı: Aranmaz'), no foreign-language minimum ('Yabancı Dil Taban Puanı: Aranmaz'), GPA floor 2.50/4.00. Foreign applicants additionally need a YÖK denklik (equivalence) certificate: 'adayların, yurtdışında lisans eğitimini tamamladıklarına dair YÖK tarafından verilmiş denklik belgesine sahip olmaları gerekir.'
liveAudition: NO instrumental performance audition — but there IS a compulsory two-stage in-person entrance exam, and Stage I is heavily ear-based, which is the practical equivalent of a barrier for him. Stage I ('I. Aşama Sınavı', 60% of the entrance score) tests six areas; 54 of its 100 points are aural: 'Müziksel İşitme' 27 puan ('Adayın dinletilen ses kaydındaki müzik ögelerini dinleyerek ayırt edebilme, özelliklerini tespit ve teknik bir dille ifade edebilme yetenekleri ölçülecektir') and 'Mesleki İşitme' 27 puan ('Adayın sınav esnasında dinletilen sesleri teknik olarak analiz, sınıflandırma ve tarif yetenekleri ölçülecektir'). It also requires reading a named Turkish-language journal article in advance and answering on it in writing, then defending that answer orally. Stage II ('II. Aşama Sınavı', 30%) is an oral defence of his submitted work. File review is only 10%.
portfolioSpec: Precise and modest. Pre-evaluation ('Ön Değerlendirme') requires him to upload, and hand the jury three printed copies of: (A) ONE single work of his own in ses kaydı / ses programlama / çalgı yapımı / ses elektroniği / akustik — a digital copy plus a written text explaining its content; (B) a digital copy of his other personal work in the field with the corresponding audio files, software or written documents and an index of them; (C) his özgeçmiş (CV). Scored out of 100: CV 33, field CV 33, work report 34. Deadline: uploaded by 23:59 on the last application day. Build brief: one deep, documented flagship piece with a written technical commentary, plus a catalogued back-catalogue.
tunisianCost: Foreign nationals (yabancı uyruklu) at the Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü: 7.500 TL + 7.500 TL = 15.000 TL per academic year (published 2024-2025 schedule, the most recent MGÜ has posted). A 2026-27 figure is UNVERIFIED — MGÜ has not published one at the URL checked. Foreign quota is small: 'YABANCI 2' places plus 1 lateral-transfer place, against 10 for Turkish nationals.
funding: Türkiye Bursları is the realistic route and he is age-eligible: the official criteria state 'For master's programs: being under the age of 30' and 'For graduate candidates: 75%' minimum academic achievement. He would be 24–26, so inside the cap. It is fully funded (tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance, one-year Turkish course, return flights) and it places the student — but it is a SEPARATE application roughly January–February, about a year and a half before he would start, and it is brutally competitive. No MGÜ-administered scholarship was found.
language: Turkish. The Sınav Kılavuzu is Turkish-only, the set reading is a Turkish journal article, and the language rule is hard: 'Eğitimini yurt dışında tamamlayan yabancı uyruklu adayların Türkçe dil seviyesini gösteren ... en az C1 seviyesinde bir belge ibraz etmeleri zorunludur.' Candidates admitted without it get one year's leave to learn Turkish: 'bu adaylar bir (1) yıl süreyle Türkçe eğitimi almak üzere izinli sayılırlar' — and are deregistered if they still lack C1 after that year. He has no Turkish.
deadline: 2026-2027 fall (PRIOR CYCLE pattern): applications 10–24 August 2026. The 2025-26 guide gives the full shape: application 29 July – 8 Aug, list of exam candidates 19 Aug, exam/interview 25 Aug, results 3 Sept, registration 8–11 Sept. Expect roughly the same late-July-to-August window in 2027 for a September 2027 start. Türkiye Bursları, if used, closes around February 2027.
verdictWhy: The degree rule is the most open he will find anywhere — 'herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak', no ALES, no language score — and it is nearly free, but the gate is an in-person Turkish-language exam whose largest single block is ear training (54 of 100 points at Stage I) and which requires him to have read a Turkish academic paper. C1 Turkish is mandatory. He has no Turkish and no trained ears; he cannot pass this in 2027. Only worth reopening if he wins Türkiye Bursları and takes the funded Turkish prep year first, which means entry in 2028, not 2027.
correction: Input gate said 'Exam/interview only'. Incomplete — there is also a scored file/portfolio submission (Ön Değerlendirme, 10% of the entrance score) with a specific spec. Input cost 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is broadly right: 15.000 TL/yr for foreign nationals on the 2024-25 schedule. The decisive fact the input misses entirely is the mandatory C1 Turkish certificate and the aural content of the exam.

programme: Master's programmes (120 ECTS, 2 yrs) — Faculty of Performing Arts / Faculty of Composition, Musicology and Music Pedag…
stillExists: YES — UNMB runs 120-ECTS / 2-year master's programmes across the Faculty of Performing Arts and the Faculty of Composition, Musicology and Music Pedagogy, with a published 2026-2027 non-EU admission methodology.
awards: Real second-cycle master's: 'Master degree, 120 ECTS - 2 years full time study'.
acceptsQuote: Formally the methodology only requires 'Sunt absolvenţi cu diplomă de licenţă sau echivalentul acesteia'. In practice every specialisation is gated by a conservatoire skill exam that a software-engineering graduate cannot sit. STIL ȘI LIMBAJ COMPOZIȚIONAL demands presentation of his own works INCLUDING 'proiectul unei lucrări vocal-simfonice de dimensiuni mai mari (cantată, oratoriu, operă de minimum 10-15 minute), o lucrare simfonică sau concertantă ... o lucrare camerală pentru ansamblu ... şi o lucrare camerală pentru instrument solo', plus a written tonal-harmony test ('Armonizarea unei teme tonale de aproximativ 16 măsuri, cu bas și sopran dat'). SINTEZA MUZICOLOGICĂ requires 'Nivelul C1 de competență lingvistică pentru limba română' as a preliminary condition. STILISTICĂ DIRIJORALĂ requires conducting from memory plus 'Solfegiu la prima vedere'. JAZZ requires 'un recital de muzică de jazz ... de aproximativ 20-25 de minute'. Muzică pop requires 'cel puţin 4 compoziţii originale, incluzând partiturile'.
liveAudition: YES — decisive. Almost every specialisation is a live, in-person performance or conducting exam in Bucharest, and even the composition track is a live defence of scored orchestral works with a written harmony paper. There is no music-technology, electronic-music or production master at UNMB at all.
portfolioSpec: Not applicable in the form he could build. Where a portfolio exists (Stil și limbaj compozițional) it must be notated concert music: a large vocal-symphonic project of at least 10–15 minutes, a symphonic or concertante work of at least 10–15 minutes, a chamber ensemble work and a solo instrumental work, and 'Nu se vor putea prezenta lucrări incomplete'. Muzică pop: at least 4 original compositions WITH SCORES and recordings.
tunisianCost: EUR 6,750 per academic year. 'Pentru anul universitar 2024/2025, taxele de școlarizare a cetățenilor străini sunt de 6750 Euro/an universitar (9 luni x 750 Euro/lună).' Paid in a single instalment for the first year.
funding: No UNMB scholarship for fee-paying non-EU students is published in the methodology. Romanian state routes (MFA scholarship, ARICE) are separate, earlier applications, not automatic on admission.
deadline: 2026-2027 (PRIOR CYCLE pattern): SESIUNEA I — 'Înscrierea candidaților: 26.06.2026-02.07.2026; Concurs: 09.07.2026-16.07.2026'. A second session is only announced if places remain.
language: Romanian. Non-EU applicants must present the Romanian preparatory-year certificate or a minimum B1 Romanian certificate from an accredited Romanian institution, a Romanian lectorate or the Institutul Cultural Român; the musicology track requires C1.
verdictWhy: UNMB has no electronic-music or music-technology master — every single specialisation is a classical or jazz performance, conducting, composition or musicology track gated by a live in-person exam in Romanian, including sight-singing, tonal harmony and orchestral scores. He fails the gate on every track. And it is not cheap: EUR 6,750/yr for a non-EU student.
correction: Input said cost 'EUR 1.5k-5k/yr' and gate 'Portfolio only'. Both wrong. Verified fee is EUR 6,750/an universitar for foreign citizens, and the gate is a live eliminatory exam ('probele concursului de admitere la studiile universitare de masterat sunt eliminatorii') requiring performance, conducting or notated symphonic composition depending on track.
